jobs.title: Sr Project Manager, CPX Bidding
jobs.description:
Why Join Us

Executive exposure: Gain visibility with senior and executive leadership and present recommendations that influence key bid and commercial decisions.
Strategic business partnerships: Work closely with the Sales VP and Unit Directors on major project opportunities and commercial strategy.
Professional development: Expand your analytical capabilities through Power BI training and development.
Remote work: Enjoy the flexibility of a remote-based position in Quebec.
Low travel expectations: Benefit from limited travel compared with a typical project management role, generally around one trip per month.
Broader commercial exposure: Build experience across bidding, estimating, contract risk, financial evaluation, construction, procurement, supply chain, and sales.
Early project influence: Help shape major wind projects before contract award by influencing cost, risk, construction strategy, and execution readiness.
Renewable energy impact: Contribute directly to the continued development of wind energy in Canada within a collaborative, international organization.

Pourquoi vous joindre à nous

Visibilité auprès de la haute direction : Profitez d’une visibilité auprès des membres de la haute direction et présentez des recommandations qui contribuent aux décisions clés liées aux appels d’offres et aux aspects commerciaux.
Partenariats stratégiques : Collaborez étroitement avec le vice-président des Ventes et les directeurs d’unité sur des occasions de projets majeurs et la stratégie commerciale.
Développement professionnel : Développez davantage vos compétences analytiques grâce à de la formation et du perfectionnement sur Power BI.
Travail à distance : Profitez de la flexibilité d’un poste en télétravail basé au Québec.
Déplacements limités : Bénéficiez d’un niveau de déplacements moins élevé que dans un rôle typique de gestion de projet, généralement environ un déplacement par mois.
Exposition commerciale élargie : Développez votre expérience en appels d’offres, estimation, risques contractuels, évaluation financière, construction, approvisionnement, chaîne d’approvisionnement et ventes.
Influence en amont des projets : Contribuez à façonner des projets éoliens majeurs avant l’attribution des contrats en influençant les coûts, les risques, la stratégie de construction et la préparation à l’exécution.
Impact dans le secteur des énergies renouvelables : Contribuez directement au développement continu de l’énergie éolienne au Canada au sein d’une organisation internationale et collaborative.

Description Du Poste

Le ou la Gestionnaire principal(e) de projet, Appels d’offres CPX
est responsable de l’alignement du périmètre de construction dans les offres et veille à ce que les engagements commerciaux soient prêts pour l’exécution. Il ou elle est responsable du positionnement des coûts de construction, de la visibilité des risques et de l’état de préparation global de l’offre pour l’exécution. Ce rôle consiste à identifier, documenter et quantifier les risques et opportunités contractuels, ainsi qu’à harmoniser les estimations des coûts de construction avec l’échéancier du projet.

Pour les conditions contractuelles non standard, le ou la Gestionnaire principal(e) de projet, Appels d’offres CPX évalue les impacts financiers associés aux écarts contractuels. Ceux-ci comprennent notamment, sans s’y limiter, la prolongation de la durée des travaux sur site, le fonctionnement en roue libre (« freewheeling ») et le stockage vertical. La personne titulaire du poste dirige la coordination interfonctionnelle afin d’obtenir les estimations justificatives requises, y compris l’obtention de soumissions de fournisseurs tiers par l’entremise des achats pour les activités EPC (ingénierie, approvisionnement et construction), le montage/l’installation, les infrastructures connexes (« balance of plant ») et les services de maintenance externes.

Responsabilités
Leadership et gestion des appels d’offres

Superviser le processus d’appel d’offres en coordonnant les contributions des différentes parties prenantes et en veillant au respect des échéanciers et des jalons.
Assumer la responsabilité du développement des propositions afin de garantir que les soumissions soient complètes, claires et conformes aux exigences.
Gérer les communications avec les clients pendant la phase d’appel d’offres, y compris les demandes d’information (RFI) et les clarifications.
Assurer l’alignement des équipes Ventes, Ingénierie, Approvisionnement et Construction autour d’une approche cohérente de soumission.
Fournir des recommandations claires à la direction et signaler les enjeux nécessitant une escalade afin de soutenir les décisions et approbations relatives aux offres.

Alignement des coûts, des risques et des aspects commerciaux

Préparer et valider les estimations de coûts de construction.
Évaluer les impacts sur les coûts et les échéanciers découlant des négociations contractuelles.
Identifier, évaluer et quantifier les risques contractuels ainsi que les écarts par rapport aux normes établies.
Communiquer clairement les hypothèses, les risques et les principaux facteurs de coûts pour approbation par la direction.

Faisabilité technique et préparation à l’exécution

Valider les hypothèses clés (logistique, installation, conditions de chantier) avec les équipes internes.
Réaliser la diligence raisonnable des sites et identifier les risques liés à la constructibilité.
Élaborer des quantités préliminaires et des intrants de coûts de haut niveau (BOM, relevés quantitatifs/takeoffs).
Contribuer à la définition des méthodes de construction et des hypothèses d’échéancier.

Transfert à l’exécution et amélioration continue

Soutenir le transfert du projet vers les équipes d’exécution, notamment en ce qui concerne le périmètre, le budget et l’alignement des risques.
Documenter clairement les hypothèses et les réserves commerciales.
Recueillir les leçons apprises et améliorer les approches futures de soumission.

Qualifications

Baccalauréat en ingénierie, gestion de la construction, gestion de projet ou dans un domaine connexe.
Minimum de 10 ans d’expérience en gestion de chantier sur des projets de génie civil lourd, d’utilités publiques, de production d’énergie ou industriels d’une valeur supérieure à 50 M$, ou au moins 5 ans d’expérience en gestion d’appels d’offres, estimation et négociation de sous-traitance pour des projets EPC éoliens, de génie civil lourd, d’utilités publiques ou industriels réalisés en auto-exécution, incluant l’évaluation financière.
Connaissance avancée de :
Le marché de la construction éolienne, les stratégies d’estimation, le contrôle des coûts et la planification;

ou

La chaîne d’approvisionnement, le transport, la modélisation financière et les contrats de projet.

Expérience démontrée dans l’utilisation efficace de logiciels d’estimation électroniques.
Connaissance des concepts, pratiques et procédures standards de l’industrie de la construction.
Maîtrise de Word, PowerPoint et Primavera (ou d’un logiciel de planification équivalent), ainsi que des compétences avancées avec Excel.

Compétences

Expérience démontrée dans la gestion ou la coordination de personnel interne, de ressources d’ingénierie, d’estimateurs, d’activités d’approvisionnement et d’entrepreneurs en construction.
Capacité à présenter des recommandations et la documentation justificative à la haute direction afin d’obtenir les approbations requises, et à défendre ses positions auprès des dirigeants et directeurs de différentes fonctions.
Capacité à maintenir un haut niveau de précision tout en travaillant dans un environnement à forte cadence.
Connaissance des principes et pratiques de gestion, de supervision et d’administration.
Excellentes habiletés de communication persuasive, avec la capacité de mobiliser des intervenants techniques et non techniques et de présenter des positions solides à la direction.
Capacité démontrée à coordonner et aligner des équipes interfonctionnelles des secteurs :
Ventes
Ingénierie
Transport
Chaîne d’approvisionnement
Approvisionnement
Construction

Capacité à gérer plusieurs priorités concurrentes et à performer efficacement dans un environnement d’appels d’offres axé sur le respect des échéances.
Livraison constante d’un travail de grande qualité avec un haut niveau de rigueur et d’attention aux détails.
Maîtrise des outils Microsoft Office, incluant des compétences avancées dans Excel.
Bilinguisme français-anglais requis, avec la capacité de gérer efficacement les relations clients et les discussions contractuelles, notamment auprès de clients situés au Québec.
Résider au Québec et posséder une bonne connaissance du marché régional et de ses intervenants.

Ce que nous offrons

Nous offrons un poste stimulant au sein d’un environnement inspirant chez le plus grand fabricant mondial d’éoliennes. Nous valorisons l’initiative, la collaboration, la responsabilisation et la rigueur. Vous évoluerez dans un contexte international axé sur la durabilité et la sécurité et travaillerez aux côtés de collègues qui se soutiennent mutuellement.

________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

Job Description:

The Sr. Project Manager, CPX Bidding owns construction scope alignment within bids and ensures execution-ready commercial commitments. Accountable for construction cost position, risk visibility, and overall bid execution readiness. This role is responsible for identifying, documenting, and quantifying contractual risks and opportunities, and for aligning construction cost estimates with the project schedule.

For non-standard contract terms, the Sr. Project Manager, CPX Bidding develops cost impacts associatedwith deviations. These include, but are not limited to, extended site duration, freewheeling, and vertical storage. The role leads cross-functional coordination to obtain supporting estimates, including securing third-party vendor quotes through procurement for EPC, erection/installation, balance of plant, and external maintenance scopes.

Responsibilities:

Bid Leadership & Ownership

Oversee the bid process, coordinating contributions and keeping teams aligned with timelines and milestones.
Own proposal development, ensuring submissions are complete, clear, and compliant.
Manage customer communications during the bid phase, including RFIs and clarifications.
Align Sales, Engineering, Procurement, and Construction with a consistent bid approach.
Provide clear recommendations and escalation points to leadership to support bid decisions and approvals.

Cost, Risk & Commercial Alignment

Prepare and validate construction cost estimates.
Assess cost and schedule impacts from contract negotiations.
Identify, evaluate, and quantify contract risks and deviations from standards.
Clearly communicate assumptions, risks, and cost drivers for leadership approval

Technical & Execution Feasibility

Validate key assumptions (logistics, installation, site conditions) with internal teams.
Perform site due diligence and identify constructability risks.
Develop high-level quantities and cost inputs (BOMs / takeoffs)
Support definition of construction approach and schedule assumptions.

Handover & Continuous Improvement

Support handover to execution teams, including scope, budget, and risk alignment.
Document assumptions and commercial qualifications clearly.
Capture lessons learned and improve future bid approaches.

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, or related field
Minimum 10 years of field-based construction management experience on heavy civil, utility, power, or industrial projects exceeding $50M; or 5+ years of bid management, estimating, and subcontract negotiation experience on EPC wind, heavy civil, utility, or industrial self-perform projects (and financial evaluation experience)
Advanced knowledge of:
Wind energy construct

jobs.title: Aviation Project Manager
jobs.description:
Ardurra is seeking an Aviation Project Manager to join our growing team in California.

At Ardurra, we’re more than an engineering and consulting firm—we’re a team dedicated to shaping the future through smart solutions and strong partnerships. Our mission is simple: empower our people to deliver innovative, sustainable projects that make a real impact on communities. Guided by our core values—Client Driven, Uniquely Nimble, Low Bureaucracy, Team Collaboration, Unlimited Opportunities, Relationship Focused, and Entrepreneurial Spirit—we foster a culture that puts people first.

Primary Function

Ardurra is looking for an Aviation Project Manager for our growing Aviation Group. In this key role, you will be responsible for overseeing projects and serving as a client manager for airport design and construction projects within specific regions. The ideal individual will provide mentoring to junior staff, lead QA/QC efforts, and play a strategic role in expanding Ardurra's aviation presence through client relationship management and business development initiatives. The ideal individual for this role will be joining a well-established aviation group with a diverse workload of airfield and airport improvement projects. From project planning, regulatory approvals, environmental compliance, financial planning, legislative strategy, land acquisition, and design phasing, this individual will be heavily involved in projects from concept through completion.

In addition to project delivery, this role will be instrumental in identifying new business opportunities, developing and maintaining relationships with airport sponsors, aviation agencies, industry partners, and supporting proposal and pursuit efforts. The Aviation Project Manager will collaborate with leadership to drive growth within targeted markets, participate in industry organizations and conferences, and help position Ardurra for upcoming aviation planning, design, and construction opportunities. Success in this role requires both strong technical expertise and a proactive approach to client development, market expansion, and strategic growth initiatives.

Primary Duties

Project management
Marketing
Client development
Staff Supervision and mentoring
Quality control of project design and contract documents
Office Support during construction

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Civil Engineering or a related field
PE License
8+ years' experience in the airport design and/or construction field, either in private industry or government service
Airport design, construction administration, and project management experience
Strong knowledge of FAA advisory circulars related to airport design and the FAA grant process
Strong computer skills
Excellent communication skills
Ability to lead and mentor existing staff and develop new staff as needed to support growth of the aviation group
Self-motivated, team-oriented individual with the ability to work on challenging projects in a team environment

Salary

$160,000 - $230,000+ (DOE)

Why Ardurra?

While Ardurra offers competitive compensation and rich benefits programs, it is our culture that truly sets us apart from our peers. We nurture a family-like culture, striving to create a work environment that is enjoyable, challenging and rewarding but also fun. We are acutely focused on developing our staff, whether through our internal Ardurra Academy or through our industry-leading Leadership program. We have made a deliberate and focused commitment to nurture a people-centric culture where people are: valued as individuals; supported in their professional and career development with multiple, varied career paths; provided the tools and resources to be successful, engaged, and satisfied in their work; and positive benefits, time-off programs, and flexibility to help maintain a healthy balance between work and home.

Ardurra is an Equal Opportunity/ Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, gender identity or sexual orientation.

NOTICE TO THIRD PARTY AGENCIES:

Ardurra does not accept unsolicited resumes from recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of a signed Agency Agreement, Ardurra will not consider or agree to payment of any referral compensation or recruiter fee. If a resume or candidate is submitted to any hiring manager without a previously signed agreement, Ardurra reserves the right to pursue and hire those candidate(s) without any financial obligation to the recruiter or agency. These candidates will be considered property of Ardurra. We’re not currently looking to add any more agencies to our list of approved vendors, so please do not contact any of our managers or recruitment team with sales calls or details of your candidates.

jobs.title: Qualitative Project Manager (Remote)
jobs.description:
M3 USA is at the forefront of healthcare innovation, offering digital solutions across healthcare, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, and more. Since our inception in 2000, we’ve seen remarkable growth, fueled by our mission to utilize the internet for a healthier world and more efficient healthcare systems.

Our success is anchored in our trusted digital platforms that engage physician communities globally, facilitating impactful medical education, precise job placement, and insightful market research. M3 USA prides itself on a dynamic and innovative work environment where every team member contributes to global health advancements.

Joining M3 USA means being part of a dedicated team striving to make a significant difference in healthcare. We provide a unique opportunity for you to be at the cutting edge of healthcare innovation, shaping the future in a meaningful career. Embrace the chance to drive change with M3 USA.

Due to our continued growth, we are hiring for a Qualitative Project Manager
at M3 Global Research
, an M3 company.

About the Business Unit:

M3 Global Research, part of M3 Inc., provides the most comprehensive and highest quality market research recruitment and support services available to the industry with relationships reaching respondents in more than 70 countries worldwide.

M3 Global Research maintains ISO 20252 and 27001 certifications with the highest quality data collection and project management capabilities that cover the spectrum of quantitative and qualitative techniques utilized today. M3 services incorporate all of the most advanced statistical and attitudinal methodologies allowing clients to provide world-class offerings and support services to their end-client customers throughout multiple industry sectors.

Job Description

Mission:

The Project Manager-Qualitative is responsible for the day-to-day management of multiple studies, both domestic and international, with a focus on qualitative research. The PM will actively and directly manage all aspects of each project, to ensure successful project completion, on time and within budget, while meeting and exceeding client expectations. The PM will work on a full team of Associate Project Managers, Project Managers, and Senior Project Managers, all of whom report to the Director of Operations.

Manage qualitative projects through entire project life cycle including all aspects of managing clients, partners and healthcare professional sample. Complete project management of quantitative projects may be expected as well.
Facilitate screening, scheduling and confirming of respondents for TDIs, focus groups, in-person IDIs, online qual interviews, etc. and ensuring all respondents are prepared according to client requirements. Ability to act quickly to replace no-shows, follow up with late respondents, send last minute materials, etc. when alerted by client/moderator.
Setup and testing of survey/screener, monitoring of statistics, managing respondent honoraria and closing/auditing/invoicing of projects in technology based system.
Coordinate and lead project kickoff meetings for all assigned studies to ensure all involved parties understand project specifications, client needs, timelines, and responsibilities.
Provide regular updates and progress reports on recruitment status to meet client needs.
Proactively identify potential fielding concerns and identify issues when in field. Partner with sales team members and operations staff to address issues and/or make recommendations to improve performance on research studies.
Manage and leverage relationships with vendors, domestic and international, to facilitate accurate and timely deliverable, communications, and issue resolution.
Manage study profitability by monitoring and accounting for all project costs affecting the budget.
Provide guidance and mentoring to members of the Market Research Project Management team as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent (preferred)
2-3 years of Market Research experience
Proven ability to manage multiple qualitative projects simultaneously in a fast-paced environment with shifting deadlines
Experience in quantitative project management (preferred)
Self-motivated with exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail
Strong written and verbal communication abilities
Advanced Microsoft Office proficiency (Excel, Outlook, Word)
Quick learner of new technologies and software platforms
Well-developed analytical and problem-solving capabilities
Ability to work both autonomously and collaboratively to meet study-specific and departmental objectives

Additional Information

Benefits:

A career opportunity with M3 USA offers competitive wages, and benefits such as:

Health and Dental
Life, Accident and Disability Insurance
Prescription Plan
Flexible Spending Account
401k Plan and Match
Paid Holidays and Vacation
Sick Days and Personal Day

*M3 reserves the right to change this job description to meet the business needs of the organization

M3 USA is an equal opportunity employer, committed to the principles of inclusion and diversity for all employees and to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment.

All employment decisions at M3 USA are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, national, social or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), age,
physical or mental disability, medical history or genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, marital status, past or present military service, family or parental status, or any other status protected by the federal, state or local laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.

jobs.title: Regional Project Manager
jobs.description:
Eaton’s North American Sales division is currently seeking a Regional Project Manager. This is a remote role supporting Eaton’s Central Region, which includes Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana, Kansas, and Ohio. Candidates may be located anywhere within these states, with a preference for individuals who live within 50 miles of an Eaton facility to support collaboration and business needs.

What You’ll Do

The primary function of a Field Based Project Manager is to create value and establish the project order management process as a key differentiator from our competitors. This position is heavily involved in the electrical and mechanical details of major strategic project order and focuses on Heavy Multitenant High Rise, Hospital, University, Commercial Construction, Data Center, Utility and Industrial Projects

The primary functions include; managing the technical aspects of major electrical assembly project orders by meeting customer specifications and timelines for products, documentation, and quality.

In This Function You Will

Utilize the Project Management team resources assigned to their project orders
Assess and apply in depth knowledge of sales planning services to internal clients in one or more specialty areas, requiring technical application
Upgrade existing processes, deploy new initiatives, and recommend new solutions based on analysis and customer trends
Ensure compliance with applicable processes and procedures to achieve business goals
Proactively use competitive information to leverage advantages of Eaton Corporation
Negotiate internally for resources and priorities needed for customers
Improve financial position for Eaton and the customer.

Qualifications

Required (Basic) Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution
Minimum 5 years’ of electrical industry experience
Possess and maintain a valid and unrestricted driver’s license
Relocation is not available. Candidates must currently reside within Minnesota, Iowa, Missouri, Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana, Kansas, or Ohio to be considered.
Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Business or Electrical Engineering
PMP Certification
Strong application of Power Engineered products
5+ years of Project Management experience

Skills

Position Criteria:

Ability to present information to others in a persuasive way, professionally and diplomatically assert the leadership role that the title project manager conveys.
Demonstrated ability to take ownership of an assignment and customer satisfaction
Ability to apply project management methodologies and strategies to reduce potential project risk throughout the duration of the project lifecycle
Capable of planning and executing presentations on specific products and services to internal and external customers in order to gain recognition and customer acceptance
Knowledge of major competitors in the market and their alignment with distributors and major customers
Knowledge on plant front-end scheduling, engineering, and manufacturing process and equipment cycle times
Posses advanced computer skills in Advanced word processing, Spreadsheet, Vista, and Bidmanager
Consistent demonstration of planning, leading, and communication results from executive changes
Ability to prioritize multiple tasks and situations to achieve superior proactive project order management and customer service
Ability to travel up to 25%

The expected annual salary range for this role is $99000 - $145000 a year. This position is also eligible for a variable incentive program.

Please note the salary information shown above is a general guideline only. Salaries are based upon candidate skills, experience, and qualifications, as well as market and business considerations.

All positions may require participation in video and in-person interviews as part of the hiring process. All candidates will be evaluated based on job-related competencies, and all candidates’ privacy rights and data security will be protected in accordance with applicable laws.

Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of an applicant's race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, marital status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

Eaton believes in second chance employment. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction history will be considered regardless of their arrest or conviction history, consistent with the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act and other local laws.

You do not need to disclose your conviction history or participate in a background check until a conditional job offer is made to you. jobs.title: eDiscovery Project Manager
jobs.description:
The Project Manager role is responsible for high level management, delegation, and execution of day-to-day e-discovery project tasks, reporting to the PM Project Director team. The role involves concurrently managing multiple projects of varying complexity. The Project Manager will collaborate with attorneys, paralegals, IT personnel, and other members of the counsel and/or client legal team to ensure the successful completion of e-discovery matters. Project Managers must also mentor, train and delegate to members of the project team.

Core Competencies (based on Consilio’s Values)

Be flexible and embrace change;
Take ownership for providing outstanding service;
Value and respect the contributions of others, building trust and relationships with stakeholders;
Take initiative, act with urgency be accountable and demonstrate unwavering commitment to do the right thing
Recognize, develop and celebrate individual and team successes;
Utilize communication best practices and active listening techniques to meet stated needs
Lead with conviction.

Responsibilities

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Cleared
jobs.description:
About Aalyria

Aalyria is a leading technology company that supplies laser communications technology and temporospatial software-defined networking platforms to the aerospace industry. With technology acquired from Google, Aalyria is at the forefront of innovation in satellite and airborne mesh networks, as well as cislunar and deep-space communications. We are revolutionizing the orchestration and management of planetary mesh networks using any radio or optical spectrum, any orbit, and any hardware across land, sea, air, and space.

Role Overview

Aalyria's Spacetime platform orchestrates highly dynamic aerospace networks using a temporospatial Software Defined Networking (SDN) approach, managing not just routing but the physical link topology and lower-layer configuration underneath it.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to own execution on one of our most sensitive customer programs, work that requires an active TS/SCI clearance

, with a polygraph strongly preferred given the access levels involved. You'll be the linchpin between Aalyria's engineering teams and a cleared government customer, driving technical tradeoffs directly rather than simply tracking them. Engineering will look to you to make sequencing, scope, and architecture-adjacent calls, and to represent program status and risk with complete accuracy to customer stakeholders who may not always have full visibility into every technical detail.

This is a role for someone who can operate independently inside a classified environment, hold their own in a room with Staff or Principal engineers, and get things done through influence rather than authority.

Key Responsibilities

End-to-End Technical Program Execution: Own program planning and execution for a classified Spacetime engineering effort, driving the work through each phase of the mission and directly resolving cross-system dependencies and technical tradeoffs, not just surfacing them for others to decide.
Cleared Customer & Stakeholder Leadership: Serve as the primary programmatic interface with a cleared government customer, communicating fluently with both technical staff and senior government stakeholders across classified and unclassified channels.
Cross-Functional Orchestration: Run the operating rhythm, such as kickoffs, technical reviews, exec readouts, that keeps Engineering, Product, and Solutions Engineering aligned on status, risk, and decisions across compartmented and uncompartmented workstreams.
Requirements Translation & Technical Judgment: Translate customer and mission requirements into actionable engineering plans. You should be able to read and critique a design document unaided, and reason in real time about latency, throughput, scaling, and failure-mode tradeoffs.
Security & Compliance Stewardship: Handle classified information and CUI correctly as a matter of course, maintain a sound personal security posture, and follow program security and export-control (ITAR/EAR) requirements without needing to be reminded. Partner closely with the FSO and IT/Cybersecurity, who are direct stakeholders in how this role is evaluated.
Contract & Financial Management: Own T&M or cost-type contract reporting requirements, including monthly labor, subcontract, hardware, and materials tracking at the Master Equipment List (MEL) level to support invoicing.
Risk & Delivery Coordination: Identify schedule, scope, and dependency risk early; escalate with context; and coordinate mitigations directly with engineering leads across development, staging, and dedicated government cloud production environments.

Required Qualifications

Active TS/SCI clearance in good standing. TS/SCI with polygraph is strongly preferred given the access levels this role requires.
5+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering program management, or a closely related role delivering complex technical platforms, ideally for U.S. Government or defense/space customers.
Demonstrated technical depth: the ability to read and critique a design document unaided, and to engage engineering teams on architecture, scaling, and failure-mode tradeoffs as a peer, not a translator.
A track record with genuinely technical programs, infrastructure migrations, API/interface contracts, cross-system dependency resolution, or multi-team technical rollouts, not just cross-functional coordination with a technical flavor.
Proven ability to influence without authority and interface confidently with senior government and customer stakeholders.
Experience managing complex project financials, resource tracking, or strict contractual reporting requirements (T&M, FFP, or cost-type contracts).
U.S. citizenship (required to hold and maintain the clearance level above).
Background in engineering, hardware/software systems, or solutions architecture, or a related field with hands-on experience running technical programs alongside engineering teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Familiarity with networking, telecom, or SDN/traffic engineering concepts.
Strong background in satellite and mission operations — early-orbit commissioning, fleet readiness, or operating in high-consequence environments.
Experience supporting programs that have transitioned from prototype to production volumes, and improving TRL/MRL along the way.
In-depth knowledge of USG acquisition processes, FAR/DFARS, and contract vehicles (BAAs, sole-source, IDIQs, OTAs).
Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related technical field — preferred, not mandatory. Equivalent hands-on technical experience is evaluated on equal footing.
Willingness to travel occasionally as program needs require.

Compensation

The base salary for this role is $187,000 – $207,000, which may vary by geographic location. Compensation also includes a competitive equity grant, an annual performance bonus, and a comprehensive benefits package. Your final offer will reflect your location, skills, qualifications, and experience.

What We Offer

Innovative Environment: Work at a cutting-edge company shaping the future of aerospace communications.
Impactful Work: Directly contribute to critical national security programs and initiatives.
Growth Opportunities: Expand your career with opportunities for professional development and advancement.
Inclusive Culture: Be part of a collaborative, supportive, and inclusive workplace where your contributions matter.
Flexibility: Flexible working arrangements including hybrid remote/in-office schedules.
Compensation and Equity: Competitive salary, comprehensive benefits (401(k), dental, vision, health, life insurance), paid time off, and equity options.

ITAR/EAR Requirements

This position involves access to export-controlled information. To comply with U.S. government export regulations, applicants must meet one of the following criteria:

Qualify as a U.S. person, which includes:
U.S. citizen or national
U.S. lawful permanent resident (green card holder)
Refugee under 8 U.S.C. 1157
Asylee under 8 U.S.C. 1158
Be eligible to access export-controlled information without requiring an export authorization.
Be eligible and reasonably likely to obtain the necessary export authorization from the appropriate U.S. government agency.

The company reserves the right to decline pursuing an export licensing process for legitimate business-related reasons.

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement

Aalyria is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Qualified applicants from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply.

The Pay Range For This Role Is

187,000 - 207,000 USD per year (Remote (DC, US))

jobs.description:
Job Summary

The (Associate) Program Manager is a critical part of IPA’s Education Sector team and will largely focus on supporting the SCALE project, a multi-country initiative, delivered with the UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCDO) and implementing partners, that scales effective education interventions. The (Associate) Program Manager manages assigned SCALE projects, coordinating principal investigators, IPA country offices, other IPA teams, implementing partners, and government stakeholders to carry out research and policy activities. The role also contributes to research design, oversight, and outputs, and works with the Education Program Director on sector agenda setting, partnership development, outreach and communications, and fundraising for new education projects and initiatives.

Responsibilities

Program management of education projects (80%)

Contribute to research design, research oversight, data analysis, and the writing of policy briefs, slide decks, and other research outputs as needed for the SCALE project.
Coordinate all project stakeholders, including principal investigators, IPA country offices, funders, implementing partners, and relevant government stakeholders, and ensure all actors are aligned on key SCALE activities, including timelines, roles, and responsibilities.
Ensure adherence to SCALE workplans and the achievement of goals and outputs as outlined in project documents and timelines, and provide regular updates (verbal and written) to the donor.
Under the supervision of the Education Program Director, work with IPA country offices and other IPA teams to develop and implement SCALE studies, including identifying clear areas of responsibility between IPA Sectors, Policy, and Right Fit Evidence teams and IPA country offices; developing efficient channels of communication; monitoring budgets and timelines; and providing technical input where required.

Outreach, strategy, and communications (10%)

Develop and coordinate SCALE and other original project communications materials (including website content, policy briefs, and research products) in collaboration with IPA’s communications and policy teams, funders, and other Education Team stakeholders.
Under the supervision of the Education Program Director, participate in external meetings, presentations, and convenings to develop key relationships with donors, sectoral partners, and senior academics around the world, and lead the tracking and documentation of those efforts in the Education Program’s Salesforce records.
Support the Education Director in updating and executing a strategic plan for IPA’s Education programs, including targets, milestones, and timelines, that demonstrate progress in relationship-building and securing funding from promising and existing donors.

Business development (10%)

Contribute to (and for selected opportunities, lead) fundraising efforts and proposal submissions by identifying funding opportunities, coordinating with principal investigators and IPA teams to develop viable research project opportunities, developing budgets, maintaining support documents, and managing proposal submissions.
Keep the Education BD tracker up to date, including progress on donor engagements, new donors identified, and progress on anticipated and active proposals, and lead agenda setting and updates to the BD team during bi-weekly Education-BD meetings.

Qualifications

Master’s degree in international public policy, (development) economics, or a related field, with coursework in quantitative methods.
At least four years of relevant work experience, including experience in education research, policy engagement, and program or research management.
Research experience and demonstrated knowledge of the education sector, research, policy, and interventions, including familiarity with randomized controlled trials (RCTs).
Experience working with bilateral funders, such as FCDO or USAID, and engaging with donors and in-country stakeholders.
Demonstrated project management skills, including strong attention to operational and research detail and the ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects efficiently with minimal supervision.
Excellent English-language communication skills and the ability to communicate effectively and clearly with internal and external stakeholders using cogent, precise, non-technical language.
Ability to present information in a structured and insightful way, both in writing and orally.
Flexibility, self-motivation, willingness to learn, and a team attitude.
Openness to occasional meetings outside regular local business hours, with notice, to accommodate colleagues in other time zones.
First-hand experience in primary data collection, including experience with both qualitative and quantitative data analysis and mixed-methods approaches (preferred).
Experience with or knowledge of education projects specifically targeting gender equality, disability, and social inclusion (GEDSI), or efforts to mainstream relevant issues (preferred).

Location

This position is open to candidates based in IPA’s country offices in Kenya, Malawi, Tanzania, Uganda, Rwanda, Zambia, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Liberia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Peru, and Colombia. Candidates without existing permanent work authorization in the country where they wish to be based will not be considered. The work environment may be office-based, hybrid, or fully remote. The role requires the ability and willingness to travel internationally (up to 20%).

Reports To

Education Program Director

Deadline to apply

November 30, 2026

About IPA

Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA) is a research and policy nonprofit that discovers and advances what works to improve the lives of people living in poverty. IPA brings together researchers and decision-makers to design, rigorously evaluate, and refine these solutions and their applications, ensuring that the evidence created is used to improve the lives of people living in poverty. In recent decades, trillions of dollars have been spent on programs designed to reduce global poverty, but clear evidence of which programs succeed is rare, and when evidence does exist, decision-makers often do not know about it. IPA exists to bring together leading researchers and these decision-makers to ensure that the evidence we create leads to a tangible impact on the world. Since its founding in 2002, IPA has worked with over 600 leading academics to conduct over 1,000 evaluations in 52 countries. This research has informed hundreds of successful programs that now impact millions of individuals worldwide.

Safeguarding at IPA

At Innovations for Poverty Action (IPA), we are committed to creating a safe and respectful environment for all individuals, particularly children and vulnerable adults. As IPA adheres to strict safeguarding principles, selected candidates will be expected to adhere to these standards. By joining IPA, you become part of a team dedicated to ethical conduct, social responsibility, and meaningful impact in the fight against global poverty. Together, we work to create a better world where everyone has the opportunity to thrive with dignity and respect.

We seek talented, passionate, and committed engineers, technologists, and business leaders to join us.

Job Summary

Supermicro is seeking an experienced Sr. Technical Program Manager to join our Solution Architecture team as the program management lead for our strategic partner solution programs. This is a solution program management role at its core: you will own the operating model, governance, and execution discipline that turn joint solution strategy with our key technology partners into predictable, well-run programs — from concept and reference architecture through validation, qualification, and customer deployment.

Working hand in hand with Solution Architects, you are the single point of program accountability across the solution lifecycle. You set the program plan and cadence, manage scope and dependencies, drive risks and decisions to closure, and keep architects, partners, sales, operations, and the factory aligned to one set of commitments. You bring the structure — intake, prioritization, milestones, change control, and reporting — that lets a portfolio of solution programs run on time and at scale.

This is a high-visibility role requiring strong program-management craft, solution and infrastructure fluency, commercial awareness, and the ability to run complex, partner-facing programs in a fast-paced environment. This role is based at our headquarters in San Jose, CA.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Own solution program management end to end — lead the full lifecycle of strategic partner solution programs, from intake and scoping through reference architecture, validation, qualification, deployment, and scale, with clear ownership of timeline, scope, and outcomes.
Define and run the program operating model — establish the planning rhythm, working cadences, decision forums, RACI, and stage gates that keep each program and the overall portfolio moving predictably.
Manage scope, schedule, and dependencies — build and maintain integrated program plans, milestones, critical paths, and cross-team dependency maps; protect commitments through disciplined change control.
Drive risk, issue, and decision management — proactively surface risks and blockers, run them to closure with clear owners and dates, and escalate with the right context at the right time.
Lead the partner program interface — serve as the primary program contact with strategic partners’ engineering, product, operations, and support teams, managing deliverables, escalations, release schedules, and joint milestones.
Coordinate solution validation and qualification programs — orchestrate partner-hosted and Supermicro-hosted validation, reliability, and proof-of-concept efforts on production-representative hardware, including the governance and traceability to run them at scale.
Orchestrate cross-functional delivery — align Solution Architecture, sales, operations, and the factory so design, material readiness, builds, and deployment stay on plan as programs move from pilot to production scale.
Establish program governance and reporting — status structures, executive dashboards, KPIs/health metrics, and operational review mechanisms that give Supermicro and partners a clear, shared view of program health.
Bridge business and technical execution — partner with account and sales-operations teams on commercial readiness (pricing inputs, SOW/agreements, forecasting, and order flow) so commercial and technical milestones stay in lockstep.
Define and track program KPIs — measure schedule adherence, milestone and qualification completion, issue burn-down, and deployment outcomes; use the data to drive continuous improvement in how programs are run.
Develop executive-level communications — program status reports, dashboards, risk assessments, and decision memos for Supermicro and partner leadership reviews.
Scale the program management practice — mature templates, playbooks, and processes so solution programs run consistently and grow cleanly from initial deployments to full production footprint.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field (Master’s degree preferred).
8+ years of experience in Technical / Solutions Program Management, with a track record of owning complex programs end to end in data center, storage, or AI infrastructure.
Deep program-management craft — integrated planning, scope and dependency management, change control, stage gates, and governance — applied across multiple concurrent programs or a program portfolio.
Proven experience running cross-functional programs that span solution design, validation, and customer deployment, ideally in partnership with external technology partners.
Strong technical fluency in data center solutions (compute, storage, and AI infrastructure) and the ability to engage credibly with Solution Architects and partner engineers.
Experience with solution validation, qualification, and NPI (New Product Introduction) processes in the server, storage, or data center industry.
Demonstrated ability to lead and influence cross-functional and partner teams in a fast-paced, dynamic environment without direct authority.
Excellent written and verbal communication, with experience producing executive-level reporting, dashboards, and decision memos.

Preferred/Bonus

Formal program/project management methodology and credentials (e.g., PMP, Agile/Scrum, or equivalent) and experience standing up program operating models and playbooks.
Experience running partner solution programs or joint validation / proof-of-concept labs with strategic technology partners.
Familiarity with storage and AI-infrastructure platforms and rack-scale solution deployment.
Exposure to the commercial side of programs — pricing, SOW/agreements, forecasting, and order flow — and comfort operating at the solution/business interface.
Background spanning the full lifecycle (product, operations, or go-to-market) that supports running programs end to end.
Willingness to travel and collaborate across global (including US–Taiwan) time zones; Mandarin proficiency a plus.

Salary Range

$160,000 - $180,000

The salary offered will depend on several factors, including your location, level, education, training, specific skills, years of experience, and comparison to other employees already in this role. In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, candidates may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as participation in bonus and equity award programs.

jobs.title: Project Manager, Pre-commercialization
jobs.description:
BUILT ON FLAVOR. FUELED BY PEOPLE.

What’s it like to work at Kinder’s? Well, there’s a lot of snacking and geeking out over what we all cooked over the weekend. Beyond that, there’s also plenty of hard work. Because we don’t just like flavor, we’re obsessed with it.

With over 100 products sold nationwide, we’re now a top-five brand in multiple flavor categories at Costco, Walmart, Whole Foods, and more. We’re not your typical CPG company. Privately held and founder-led, we like to think of ourselves as a pirate ship in a sea of cruise ships. Our crew is adventurous and fearless. We chart our own course and chase big ideas to make food unforgettable.

As we expand globally and approach $1 billion in revenue, we need more smart-and-scrappy, flavor-obsessed people to come aboard. If you’re looking for a place where you can see the real impact of your work... this is it!
Every day, you’ll be part of a journey to add flavor to millions of meals and lives.

How You Will Have An Impact At Kinder’s

The Pre-Commercialization Project Manager plays a critical role in helping Kinder's bring innovation to life by guiding new product opportunities through the earliest stages of development. You'll help build confidence that great ideas can become great products - ones that meet Kinder's high standards, delight our consumers, and can be successfully brought to market.

Working closely with the Senior Pre-Commercialization Project Manager, you'll guide innovation projects through discovery, feasibility, validation, and development. You'll bring the right people and information together, ask the questions that need to be answered, and connect the dots across functions to help teams make informed decisions and keep projects moving forward.

Pre-Commercialization is an exciting and critical step in bringing Kinder's innovation to life - where we build confidence in whether an opportunity is worth pursuing, whether we can create a product that meets our high standards and consumers' expectations, and whether we have the capabilities to successfully bring it to market. This role requires a balance of structure and agility: applying rigor where it adds value, adapting as we learn, and maintaining a bias toward action.

You'll own portfolio-level PMO analytics across all pre-commercialization projects, translating project data into clear insights that improve visibility, prioritization, resource planning, and decision-making.

You'll partner closely with Culinary, Innovation, R&D, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, and Commercialization to help turn promising ideas into products we're proud to put the Kinder's name on.

What You'll Be Doing

Guide Innovation Through Pre-Commercialization

Manage a portfolio of innovation projects through discovery, feasibility, validation, and development.
Bring cross-functional teams together to clarify objectives, answer critical questions, and determine what is needed to move opportunities forward.
Proactively seek out information, surface gaps, and connect inputs across functions to develop a clear and cohesive picture of each opportunity.
Maintain momentum by driving actions, decisions, and accountability while adapting as new information and learnings emerge.

Guide Readiness and Feasibility

Guide cross-functional teams in evaluating the relevant feasibility considerations for each opportunity, including culinary, technical, operational, supply chain, financial, and commercial needs.
Ensure teams have the information needed to determine whether concepts can deliver against Kinder's standards and consumer expectations while being viable to commercialize.
Identify and clarify key risks, assumptions, dependencies, capabilities, and open questions that need to be addressed.
Help teams synthesize information and navigate trade-offs to support thoughtful, timely decisions.

Drive Project Planning and Cross-Functional Alignment

Develop and maintain clear project plans in Wrike, including key deliverables, milestones, decisions, risks, and ownership.
Lead project meetings, feasibility reviews, and cross-functional alignment sessions that drive decisions and action.
Communicate project status, decisions, risks, and next steps clearly across teams.
Proactively work through roadblocks and ensure stakeholders understand what's needed to keep projects moving.
Facilitate effective handoff to Commercialization Project Managers with clear alignment and documentation of key decisions, assumptions, and requirements.

Own Portfolio Analytics and PMO Reporting

Own and maintain PMO analytics across all pre-commercialization projects, providing a consistent and accurate view of portfolio health, stage, timelines, milestones, risks, dependencies, decisions, and resource needs.
Develop and maintain portfolio dashboards, reports, and key performance indicators in Wrike and related tools to identify trends, bottlenecks, capacity constraints, and opportunities for improvement.
Analyze project and portfolio data and translate it into actionable insights and recommendations that support leadership decisions, project prioritization, resource allocation, and timely escalation.
Establish clear data standards and reporting cadences, and partner with project owners to ensure portfolio information is complete, current, and reliable.

Strengthen How We Work

Leverage established Pre-Commercialization tools and frameworks to bring appropriate structure and consistency to project evaluation.
Identify practical opportunities to improve tools, processes, and ways of working based on project learnings and organizational needs.
Capture and share learnings that strengthen future innovation projects and cross-functional collaboration.

What You Bring To The Table

You’ve led pre-commercialization projects tied to manufacturing, supply chain, commercialization, or operational execution
. If your background is primarily in software product management or creative agency/marketing PM work, this role will NOT
be the right fit.

Action-oriented and comfortable making progress in the face of ambiguity and incomplete information.
Strong situational awareness and business judgment, with the ability to know when to dig into the details and when to zoom out and connect the broader picture.
Naturally curious and resourceful - you ask thoughtful questions, chase down information, and bring disparate inputs together to get to the answers teams need.
Practical problem-solver who anticipates risks and downstream implications and works collaboratively to find a path forward.
Clear, thoughtful communicator who listens to understand, builds trust across functions, and drives clarity, alignment, and momentum.
Able to apply structure and rigor where it adds value without creating unnecessary complexity.
Flexible and highly situationally aware, with the ability to read the room and adapt your approach to different people, situations, and changing priorities while maintaining strong relationships and forward momentum.
Deep interest in how great food ideas become products that consumers love.

Skills / Experience

7+ years of experience in project management, innovation, product development, or cross-functional program management, ideally within a CPG, food, or beverage company.
Experience guiding innovation projects through early-stage development, feasibility assessment, and commercialization readiness.
Strong project planning, stakeholder management, problem-solving, and decision-support skills.
Demonstrated experience owning portfolio-level PMO analytics across multiple projects, including building dashboards and KPIs, monitoring portfolio health and capacity, identifying trends and risks, and translating data into actionable recommendations for leadership.
Proven ability to coordinate and influence cross-functional teams, coupled with a strong understanding of the breadth of work, priorities, constraints, and interdependencies across Culinary, R&D, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, and Marketing.
Experience with project management platforms such as Wrike, Smartsheet, Monday.com, or similar tools.
Experience working in fast-paced, entrepreneurial, or high-growth environments preferred.

Personal Characteristics

High ownership and accountability.
Resourceful, adaptable, and comfortable operating in dynamic environments.
Strong sense of urgency paired with thoughtful judgment.
Values progress over perfection and knows when to make a call and move forward.
Hungry to learn, grow, and contribute to a high-performing innovation function.
Obsessed with flavor and excited to help build the future of Kinder's product portfolio.

Location + Pay Transparency:

This role will be located in our Walnut Creek, California office. The expected starting salary range for this role is $135,000- $155,000 per year. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range based on the location of the role. The amount a particular employee will earn within the salary range will be based on factors such as relevant education, qualifications, performance and business needs.

Seasoned For Success

No two days here are the same.
We try to be good team members and good communicators, but we don’t live by hierarchy and structure – everyone is a difference maker here.
We make a lot of decisions in the face of incomplete information – our team embraces ambiguity and tries to make good decisions fast rather than great decisions slow.
We believe our job is to take smart risk, not to eliminate risk.
We believe in growing our skills and becoming a better company with more managerial expertise, but we are an entrepreneurial company at heart.
We aren’t trying to be average – we want to do exceptional things, and we are willing to work hard to achieve them.

Benefits That Bring More To The Table

We offer a range of total rewards that may include paid time off, 401k, bonus / incentive eligibility, equity grants, competitive health benefits, and other family-friendly benefits, including parental leave. Kinder’s benefits vary based on eligibility and can be reviewed in more detail during the interview process.

Our Recipe For Balance

We believe great culture starts with people. We’re a people-first company built on connection, collaboration, and balance. Most of our work happens in the office to spark creativity and community, but we also offer flexibility so team members have the autonomy to work outside the office when needed to support their work-life balance and personal commitments.

Where Every Ingredient Matters

jobs.title: Sr. Program Manager - Network Switching Total Solutions
jobs.description:
Job Req ID: 28869

About Supermicro

Supermicro® is a Top Tier provider of advanced server, storage, and networking solutions for Data Center, Cloud Computing, Enterprise IT, Hadoop/ Big Data, Hyperscale, HPC and IoT/Embedded customers worldwide. We are the #5 fastest growing company among the Silicon Valley Top 50 technology firms. Our unprecedented global expansion has provided us with the opportunity to offer a large number of new positions to the technology community. We seek talented, passionate, and committed engineers, technologists, and business leaders to join us.

Job Summary

Supermicro is seeking a Sr. Program Manager to lead operations, program, and project management for the Network Switching Total Solutions team. You will own the team’s operating model, which covers how the team plans, commits, delivers, and improves. You will also run the program portfolio across all customers, partners, and internal engagements, and manage individual projects from intake to verified close.

In This Role You Will

Design, run, and enforce the operating model and team cadence: daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly business reviews.
Manage a portfolio of concurrent programs and projects with clear owners, acceptance criteria, dates, and dependencies across the US, Taiwan, and India.
Track every commitment, flag risks before dates slip, and escalate with an agreed recovery plan.
Report delivery performance and progress toward the team’s mission to senior leadership.
Drive continuous improvement through root-cause reviews and process changes.

This role is based at Supermicro headquarters in San Jose, CA.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Includes the following essential duties and responsibilities (other duties may also be assigned):

Build the Operating Model: Turn the team charter, service catalog, role matrix, processes, and templates into one documented system, with a named owner and a current version for each piece.
Run the Team Cadence: Lead daily commitment board reviews, weekly check-ins with written recaps, monthly business reviews, and quarterly business reviews with senior leadership.
Enforce Standards: Audit adherence to the operating model every week, report gaps to the Senior Director with an owner for each fix, and hold the team to its agreed standards.
Commitment Tracking: Own every commitment board and service catalog request. Log each ask within one business day with an owner, acceptance criteria, and a due date, and close it only with acceptance evidence attached. Nothing is deleted.
Risk and Escalation: Flag at-risk dates before they slip and agree on a new date with the requestor.
Cross-Functional Dependencies: Chase open dependencies with product management, testing, RACK, SONiC, and the teams in Taiwan and India until they clear.
Reporting: Publish a weekly report of commitments met, at risk, and missed, along with progress toward the mission and mission objectives.
Root-Cause Review and Process Improvement: Review every missed commitment within five business days, find the cause, and record the process change in the operating model.
Training Coordination: Plan and schedule the team training program, assign an owner to each session, and track completion.

Qualifications

8+ years in operations management, program management, project management, or PMO roles, ideally in networking, data center, or AI infrastructure organizations.
Bachelor's degree in business, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Proven track record designing processes, templates, and operating rhythms that teams actually adopt.
Strong command of Smartsheet or a comparable work management tool, including dashboards and reporting.
Experience managing many concurrent projects and dependencies across functions and time zones (US, Taiwan, India).
Strong communication and leadership: clear written and verbal communication, the ability to hold peers and senior engineers to agreed standards, and the ability to brief senior executives.
Working knowledge of data center networking, enough to follow engineering discussions and judge when a dependency is real.

Preferred Certifications (one Or More)

Project management: PMP
Program management: PgMP or SAFe (Leading SAFe, SAFe Scrum Master, SAFe POPM, or SPC)
Agile delivery: PMI-ACP, PSM I/II/III, CSM, A-CSM, or CSP-SM
Operations management: Uptime Institute AOS, or a Lean Six Sigma Green or Black Belt

Salary Range

$150,000-$160,000

The salary offered will depend on several factors, including your location, level, education, training, specific skills, years of experience, and comparison to other employees already in this role. In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, candidates may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as participation in bonus and equity award programs.

jobs.description:
Category/Area of Expertise:
IT & Technology

Job Requisition:
566504

Address:
USA-MA-Quincy-1385 Hancock Street

OCIO - Budget & Financial Mgmt (5175549)

Ahold Delhaize USA, a division of global food retailer Ahold Delhaize, is part of the U.S. family of brands, which includes five leading omnichannel grocery brands - Food Lion, Giant Food, The GIANT Company, Hannaford and Stop & Shop. Our associates support the brands with a wide range of services, including Finance, Legal, Sustainability, Commercial, Digital and E-commerce, Technology and more.

Tech Risk Program Manager I leads the enterprise Technology Risk Management program by establishing and governing processes for risk identification, assessment, reporting, and treatment across technology domains. Partners with business and technology leaders to drive risk ownership, maintain risk registers, develop mitigation strategies, and provide actionable risk insights that enable informed decision-making, regulatory compliance, and the achievement of strategic business objectives.

Our flexible/hybrid work schedule includes 3 in-person days at one of our core locations and 2 remote days.
Our core office locations include Salisbury, NC and Quincy, MA.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis.

Duties & Responsibilities:

Risk Governance & Strategy

Lead the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Technology Risk Management program across infrastructure, applications, data, cybersecurity, privacy, and third-party technology domains.
Establish and maintain a consistent methodology for identifying, assessing, documenting, treating, and monitoring technology risks.
Partner with Technology and Business leaders to align risk management activities with organizational objectives, risk appetite, and regulatory obligations.
Facilitate cross-functional risk governance forums and working sessions to drive accountability and informed risk-based decision making.

Risk Identification & Assessment

Develop and execute risk discovery processes to proactively identify emerging, existing, and potential technology risks across portfolios, programs, products, and operational environments.
Facilitate risk identification workshops, control assessments, maturity reviews, and risk-focused project reviews with technology and business stakeholders.
Analyze risk trends, control weaknesses, audit findings, incidents, and regulatory changes to identify new or evolving risk exposures.
Partner with application owners, infrastructure teams, cybersecurity, data teams, and business functions to evaluate likelihood, impact, and residual risk ratings.

Risk Register Management

Develop enterprise standards, procedures, and guidance for the creation, maintenance, and governance of technology risk registers.
Establish risk taxonomy, scoring criteria, reporting standards, and risk ownership requirements.
Govern the quality, accuracy, completeness, and timeliness of risk register updates across technology organizations.
Monitor risk register adherence and provide challenge, oversight, and guidance to ensure risks are appropriately documented and evaluated.
Produce executive-level reporting and dashboards highlighting top risks, trends, aging actions, and treatment progress.

Risk Treatment & Remediation Management

Partner with risk owners to determine appropriate treatment strategies, including mitigation, transfer, acceptance, or avoidance.
Facilitate the development of actionable risk treatment plans with clearly defined milestones, owners, target completion dates, and success measures.
Track and report remediation progress, escalating overdue or high-risk action plans to appropriate governance bodies.
Review mitigation effectiveness and validate that implemented controls adequately reduce residual risk to an acceptable level.
Ensure dependencies, resource requirements, and implementation risks are identified and managed throughout remediation activities.

Training & Risk Culture

Design and deliver training programs that build risk management capabilities across technology and business teams.
Educate leaders, risk owners, and project teams on risk identification techniques, risk assessment methodologies, risk register usage, and treatment planning.
Promote a culture of proactive risk ownership and accountability through coaching, workshops, and awareness initiatives.
Serve as a trusted advisor to stakeholders regarding risk management best practices, governance requirements, and compliance expectations.

Compliance, Controls & Assurance

Support alignment with established risk and control frameworks, including NIST, COBIT, ISO 27001, and IT General Controls (ITGCs).
Partner with Internal Audit, Cybersecurity, Compliance, and Technology teams to address findings, control gaps, and emerging regulatory requirements.
Monitor key risk indicators (KRIs) and control performance metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of the overall risk management program.
Support audit and assessment activities by providing evidence of risk management practices, treatment plans, and governance processes.

Reporting & Executive Communications

Prepare and present risk summaries, metrics, trends, and remediation status reports for leadership and governance committees.
Develop meaningful risk analytics that support prioritization of investments, control improvements, and strategic decision making.
Communicate material technology risks, treatment recommendations, and residual risk exposure to senior leadership in a clear and actionable manner

Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of work experience..
8+ years of experience in project or program management.
Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and managing enterprise technology risk management programs.
Experience facilitating risk identification, risk assessment, and risk treatment activities across technology and business organizations.
Proven ability to establish and govern risk registers, including development of risk taxonomies, scoring methodologies, ownership models, and reporting standards.
Experience partnering with business leaders, technology owners, cybersecurity teams, application owners, infrastructure teams, and project delivery organizations to identify and manage risk.
Strong understanding of technology risk frameworks and control environments, including NIST, COBIT, ISO 27001, IT General Controls (ITGCs), and enterprise risk management practices.
Experience developing risk treatment plans and driving remediation activities through completion.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess complex technology environments and determine business impacts of risk exposures.
Experience developing executive-level reporting, risk dashboards, key risk indicators (KRIs), and governance committee materials.
Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and drive accountability without direct authority.
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to translate technical risks into business impacts and recommendations.
Experience designing and delivering training programs related to risk management processes, risk assessments, risk registers, and compliance requirements.
Experience supporting internal audits, external audits, regulatory assessments, and remediation activities.
Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple risk initiatives, priorities, and stakeholder groups simultaneously.
Proficiency with GRC platforms and risk management tools such as ServiceNow GRC, Archer, or equivalent solutions.

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience implementing or maturing technology risk management frameworks and governance programs.
Experience with risk data visualization and reporting tools such as Power BI or similar analytics platforms.
Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control (CRISC)
Experience operating within large-scale, complex enterprise environments.
Experience supporting regulatory or compliance requirements including SOX, PCI DSS, privacy regulations, cybersecurity assessments, and third-party risk management programs.

Salary Range: $136,160-$204,240

jobs.title: Information Security Manager - Identity and Access Management (IAM)
jobs.description:
We are seeking an experienced IT Information Security Manager to own, advance, and scale our Identity & Access Management (IAM) program. In this role, you will lead a dedicated team of IAM engineers and analysts responsible for identity governance, access lifecycle management, privileged access management (PAM), and authentication architecture across enterprise applications, cloud infrastructure, and hybrid environments. You will bridge strategic vision with technical execution—ensuring seamless user access while maintaining a robust zero-trust security posture and meeting stringent compliance requirements.

In This Role, You Will...

Strategic Leadership & Governance

IAM Strategy: Lead the definition, rollout, and execution of the enterprise IAM roadmap, aligning identity practices with Zero Trust principles and corporate security standards.
Governance & Policies: Develop, maintain, and enforce identity policies, including Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC), Least Privilege, and Separation of Duties (SoD).
Team Management: Lead, mentor, and build a high-performing team of IAM engineers, system integrators, and security analysts.

Operational Excellence & Technical Oversight

Lifecycle Management: Oversee the Joiner, Mover, and Leaver (JML) processes to automate provisioning and de-provisioning workflows across on-premises and cloud platforms.
Authentication & SSO: Architect and oversee modern authentication standards, including Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), SAML 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and passwordless technology.
Privileged Access Management (PAM): Manage enterprise PAM solution implementation, securing administrative credentials, session monitoring, and just-in-time access controls.
Identity Governance & Administration (IGA): Direct user access reviews, entitlement certification campaigns, and automated access request/approval workflows.

Risk Management, Compliance & Support

Audit & Compliance: Function as the primary IAM lead for internal and external audits, ensuring timely remediation of access-related findings.
Incident Response: Act as an escalation point for identity-focused security incidents, credentials compromise, and unauthorized access investigations.
Vendor Management: Evaluate, select, and manage third-party IAM software vendors, tools, and professional services partners.

Qualifications

8+ years of total experience in IT and Cybersecurity, with at least 3+ years in a leadership/management capacity focused specifically on Identity & Access Management.
Hands-on experience with industry-standard IAM tools: ○ Directory & Identity Providers: Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD), Okta, Ping Identity, Active Directory. ○ IGA Platforms: SailPoint, Saviynt, or Microsoft Entra ID Governance. ○ PAM Solutions: CyberArk, BeyondTrust, Delinea, or HashiCorp Vault.
Deep understanding of OAuth 2.0, SAML, OIDC, SCIM, Kerberos, and LDAP protocols.
Strong familiarity with regulatory compliance frameworks.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus Qualifications

CISSP, CISM, CISA, or vendor-specific certifications (e.g., Okta Certified Professional, Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate, SailPoint Certified).
Hands-on experience managing identity across AWS, Azure, or GCP cloud environments.
Proficiency in scripting/automation (PowerShell, Python, REST APIs) for workflow optimization.

$228,000 - $273,000 a year

Base Salary Range

There are three major components to compensation for this position: salary, Amazon Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), and Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights. A sign-on bonus may be offered as part of the compensation package. The listed range applies only to the base salary. Compensation will vary based on geographic location and level. Leveling, as well as positioning within a level, is determined by a range of factors, including, but not limited to, a candidate's relevant years of experience, domain knowledge, and interview performance. The salary range listed in this posting is representative of the range of levels Zoox is considering for this position.

Zoox also offers a comprehensive package of benefits, including paid time off (e.g. sick leave, vacation, bereavement), unpaid time off, Zoox Stock Appreciation Rights, Amazon RSUs, health insurance, long-term care insurance, long-term and short-term disability insurance, and life insurance.

Zoox is developing the first ground-up, fully autonomous vehicle fleet and the supporting ecosystem required to bring this technology to market. Sitting at the intersection of robotics, machine learning, and design, Zoox aims to provide the next generation of mobility-as-a-service in urban environments.
